body:
Neither checks _disconnected, so an ElectrumBackend reconnect monitor still ticking after wallet.stop() puts the stopped instance back into the header and script hash routers and _onNewBlock then refreshes a shut-down wallet. The window is small because LightningNode.destroy() calls stopReconnectMonitor() before wallet.stop(), but the guard is inconsistent with the one the restore path got.

Found while working on #482.
title: Public subscribeToHeader/subscribeToAddresses re-register an instance disconnect()...

body:
restoreSubscriptions returns (resolves) rather than throwing when _disconnected is set, so restoreSubscriptionsBestEffort's catch never re-adds the network, leaving other instances' script hashes unrestored. In practice disconnect() also calls electrum.stop(), so surviving instances hit checkConnection's unconditional restore within POLLING_INTERVAL (10s), which is why this is not blocking.

Found while working on #482.
title: A disconnect landing mid-restore drops the network's restore debt instead of re-arming it

body:
restoreSubscriptions uses Promise.all, so one failing script hash aborts the rest of the restore including the wallet's own subscribeToAddresses({}), and the re-armed subscriptionRestoreOwed entry is consumed only in _doConnect or checkConnection's reconnect branch, neither of which runs while pings keep succeeding. Master had the same silent loss via `void this.subscribeToAddresses({})`, so this is an incomplete improvement rather than a regression; checkConnection could also discharge the debt on its healthy path.

Found while working on #482.
title: A failed restore is only retried by a later reconnect, which a healthy link never triggers

body:
`await electrum.stop()` defaults to the module-global clients.network, so in a process with two Electrum instances on different networks a disconnect can tear down the other network's client, and unlike the new failover teardown it never adds to subscriptionRestoreOwed. The line predates this PR; recovery still happens via the 10s checkConnection poll.

title: disconnect() stops electrum for clients.network, not this.electrumNetwork, and records...

body:
When a candidate equals the connected peer, stopPeerIfServerChanged skips teardown, but rn-electrum-client's connectToPeer pings and calls disconnectFromPeer itself, wiping subscribedAddresses/onAddressReceive with clientReset false; if that candidate then fails and rotation lands on a different server, _doConnect re-issues headers but never the script hashes. checkConnection's unconditional restore covers the polling path, so this only bites a direct connectToElectrum() call over a multi-server list, and master lost those subscriptions too.

title: Client-internal reconnect clears the same bookkeeping without recording a restore debt

body:
When teardown is refused, the old peer and handler remain live, but the failed candidate loop publishes a disconnected state. A focused HEAD test confirmed `connectedToElectrum` became false while the retained peer still handled notifications.

title: Failed switch reports a live peer as disconnected

body:
The initial header restore and the daemon resubscribe can overlap before the dependency marks headers subscribed. A focused probe registered two listeners and sent two header subscription requests, causing duplicate notification processing.

Found while working on #482.
title: Failover can install duplicate header listeners

body:
When stopPeerIfServerChanged refuses every candidate, _doConnect falls through to publishConnectionChange(false) and sets connectedToElectrum = false even though the old connection is intact and still serving RPCs, and this.servers has already been overwritten to the new target at lines 289-291, so every later guarded call retries the same doomed switch. close() throwing is unlikely (it is conn?.end()/conn?.destroy()), so the practical exposure is small, but the reported state contradicts the deliberate decision to keep the working peer.

Found while working on #482.
title: A refused teardown marks the wallet disconnected while the peer is still live

body:
restoreSubscriptions deliberately re-issues the whole shared per-network script hash router so other Electrum instances keep their subscriptions, but the header subscription is re-issued only by `this.subscribeToHeader()` in _doConnect, and the client keeps one header handler per network (subscribeHeader answers "Already Subscribed." to everyone else). With more than one Wallet on a network the resetting instance captures newBlock delivery and the others go silent until their own reconnect path fires; not a regression, since after a swap master delivered headers to nobody.

Found while working on #482.
title: Headers are restored only for the instance that reset the client

body:
rn-electrum-client's connectToPeer pings a same-target peer and, on failure, runs disconnectFromPeer (clearing subscribedAddresses/subscribedHeaders/onAddressReceive) before building a new client, but stopPeerIfServerChanged returns clientReset:false for that case, so _doConnect re-issues only headers; any reconnect reached through the `if (!this.connectedToElectrum) await this.connectToElectrum(...)` guards in getAddressBalance/getAddressHistory therefore loses every script hash. checkConnection covers the polling path explicitly, so the hole is narrow, and it predates this PR, but calling restoreSubscriptions unconditionally after a successful connect (it is idempotent and answers "Already Subscribed." for known hashes) would close it inside the machinery this PR adds.
